plan.contextChunk: This figure sets two congruent parallelograms side by side, outlined in dark blue with both diagonals drawn as thin lines, to place vector addition next to vector subtraction. In the left parallelogram the bottom edge carries an orange arrowhead pointing right and is labeled u; the slanted right-hand edge carries an orange arrowhead pointing up and to the right and is labeled v; and the diagonal running from the lower-left corner to the upper-right corner ends in an orange arrowhead and is labeled u + v. The right parallelogram repeats the same outline, but its top edge is the one labeled u with an orange arrowhead pointing right, its slanted right-hand edge carries an orange arrowhead pointing down and to the right and is labeled -v, its bottom edge is also labeled u, and the diagonal that descends from the upper-left corner toward the lower-right corner is labeled u - v. Drawing both results inside the same shape shows that the sum and the difference are simply the two diagonals of one parallelogram. The pairing makes the point that u - v is built by reversing v and joining it head to tail with u.

interactionPlan.concept: In a parallelogram built from u and v, the two diagonals are the resultants u + v and u − v, so subtracting a vector is the same as adding its reverse.
elements: Left parallelogram: dark navy outline, lower-left origin point, horizontal bottom edge, slanted right edge rising to upper right
Left parallelogram both diagonals drawn as thin navy lines (lower-left to upper-right, and upper-left to lower-right)
Left: orange arrowhead on bottom edge pointing right, italic label 'u' below it
Left: orange arrowhead on slanted right edge pointing up-and-right, italic label 'v' beside it
Left: orange arrowhead at the upper-right end of the main diagonal, italic label 'u + v' along the diagonal
Right parallelogram: identical navy outline and both thin diagonals
Right: orange arrowhead on top edge pointing right, italic label 'u' above it
Right: orange arrowhead on slanted right edge pointing down-and-right, italic label '−v' beside it
Right: italic label 'u' below the bottom edge (translated copy of u)
Right: descending diagonal from upper-left toward lower-right with orange arrowhead, italic label 'u − v'
Shared tail vertex marked at lower-left of each figure
Ghosted dashed copy of v (when reversed) to show −v is v flipped
Legend/caption strip: orange = active vectors and resultant, navy = parallelogram frame

interactions.label: Operation
interactions.teaches: Reversing v to −v swaps which diagonal of the very same parallelogram is the resultant, so subtraction is addition of the opposite vector.

interactions.label: Construction step
interactions.teaches: The resultant is the end product of a head-to-tail construction: place u, attach v (or −v) at its head, close the parallelogram, and the diagonal from the common tail is the answer.
Each diagonal belongs to a specific pair of edge vectors — clicking one lights up the two sides that generate it, showing u + v and u − v live in the same figure.

demo_steps.title: Start with u
demo_steps.narration: A single vector u is drawn from the origin along the bottom edge, orange arrowhead pointing right. Nothing else exists yet.

demo_steps.title: Attach v head to tail
demo_steps.narration: v is placed with its tail at the head of u, slanting up and to the right. The two vectors now form a bent path from the origin.

demo_steps.title: Close the parallelogram
demo_steps.narration: Copies of u and v complete the figure, so the same endpoint is reached by going u-then-v or v-then-u.

demo_steps.title: The sum is the long diagonal
demo_steps.narration: The diagonal from the common tail to the opposite corner is highlighted in orange and labeled u + v.

demo_steps.title: Reverse v into −v
demo_steps.narration: Flipping the toggle turns v around: the arrowhead on the slanted edge now points down and to the right, labeled −v, while u is unchanged.

demo_steps.title: The difference is the other diagonal
demo_steps.narration: Head-to-tail with −v, the resultant becomes the descending diagonal labeled u − v — the same parallelogram, the other diagonal.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: One parallelogram holds both answers: its two diagonals are u + v and u − v, because subtracting v is just adding the reversed vector −v.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Two congruent slanted parallelograms side by side on white, each outlined in thick dark navy (#1F4E79) with both diagonals drawn as thin navy lines. The shape leans right: horizontal bottom edge, right edge slanting up-right at roughly 60°. Active vectors and the active resultant are drawn in orange (#E8601C) with solid triangular arrowheads placed mid-edge or at the edge's end; inactive edges stay plain navy. Labels are bold italic serif letters (u, v, −v, u + v, u − v) set just outside their edge or alongside the diagonal. Left figure = addition: u on the bottom edge pointing right, v on the right edge pointing up-right, u + v along the lower-left-to-upper-right diagonal. Right figure = subtraction: u on the top edge pointing right, −v on the right edge pointing down-right, a second u label under the bottom edge, and u − v along the upper-left-to-lower-right diagonal. When the toggle animates, keep the outline fixed and only spin the v arrowhead 180° plus swap which diagonal is orange; a faint dashed ghost of the original v can remain to make the reversal visible. Clicking a diagonal thickens it and tints its two generating edges the same orange while dimming the rest.
interactionPlan.figureCaption: Vector addition and subtraction as the two diagonals of one parallelogram.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Toggle between addition and subtraction: the learner switches the parallelogram from u + v to u - v, v reverses into -v and the active diagonal changes, and subtraction becomes addition of the opposite vector.
- Button for construction steps: the learner steps through drawing u, placing v or -v head-to-tail, completing the parallelogram, and revealing the diagonal, making the result vector depend on the order of geometric construction.
- Click on a diagonal: the learner selects either resultant diagonal, that diagonal and its component edges highlight, and the relationship between each diagonal and its pair of side vectors becomes clear.

authoredContext:
Vector subtraction is similar to vector addition. To find u − v, view it as u + (−v). Adding −v is reversing direction of v and adding it to the end of u. The new vector begins at the start of u and stops at the end point of −v. See the figure for a visual that compares vector addition and vector subtraction using parallelograms.

Showing vector addition and subtraction with parallelograms. For addition, the base is u, the side is v, the diagonal connecting the start of the base to the end of the side is u+v. For subtraction, thetop is u, the side is -v, and the diagonal connecting the start of the top to the end of the side is u-v.

discrepancies: The SVG viewBox (620×200) is letterboxed inside a much taller container, so the two parallelograms render as a small band with a large empty area above and below; the source figure fills its frame and the marks read noticeably larger.

In the right (difference) panel the −v arrowhead and the u−v diagonal arrowhead end up very close together near the bottom-right corner, producing a cluttered double-arrow cluster where the source separates the edge arrow from the diagonal head.

Label sizes (≈15px in a 620-wide viewBox) come out small on screen; the primary annotations 'u + v' / 'u − v' do not stand out from the 'u' / 'v' edge labels the way they do in the printed figure, where the resultant label is the visual focus.

Guided/step modes fade the non-active parallelogram to opacity 0.15, effectively removing half the printed two-panel composition; this is a reasonable teaching choice but departs from the source layout whenever any control is touched.
A dashed peach 'ghost v' arrow is added in the difference panel during guided steps — a pedagogically sensible addition but not present in the source figure.
evaluation.notes: Structurally faithful two-panel parallelogram-rule figure with correct navy frames, partial orange edge arrows, both diagonals and correct u/v/−v/u+v/u−v labelling, backed by genuinely useful step-player, toggle, construction-step and clickable-diagonal interactions; main weaknesses are the small letterboxed artwork with wasted vertical space, slightly small label hierarchy, and arrowhead crowding at the bottom-right of the difference panel.
action_items: Enlarge the drawing: set the viewBox aspect closer to the container (or scale the panel coordinates up) so the parallelograms fill the available width/height like the printed figure instead of sitting in a thin band.
Increase label font size and give the resultant labels ('u + v', 'u − v') a heavier/larger treatment than the edge labels to match the source's visual hierarchy.
Shift the u−v diagonal arrowhead (or shorten the −v edge arrow) so the two orange heads in the right panel do not overlap near the bottom-right vertex.
In guided steps, dim the inactive panel less aggressively (e.g. opacity 0.35) or keep its navy outline visible so the two-panel composition of the source is still legible.

feedback.rationale: Concept and interaction structure are correct (concept 5, no failure modes, empty plan action items); remaining issues are implementation-level — viewBox scaling, label sizing/hierarchy, arrowhead overlap, and dimming opacity.

The lower (difference) panel adds a bold orange arrowhead on the descending u − v diagonal; in the source that diagonal is a plain thin navy line and only the u and −v edge arrows are orange, so the generated panel over-emphasises the resultant relative to the original.

The 'u + v' label sits directly on the crossing of the two diagonals rather than clearly above the sum diagonal as in the source; the white halo rescues legibility but the placement reads as a mild collision with the artwork.
Minor additions not in the source: a navy 'common tail' dot and a dashed ghost copy of v appear in guided/stepped states (acceptable pedagogically, but they are extra elements).

Vector proportions/arrow lengths differ slightly — in the source the orange u and v arrows are short sub-segments near the middle/end of their edges, while here the orange arrows for the active panel span nearly whole edges in some steps.

discrepancies: Left panel's primary label 'u + v' is placed at about one-third along the diagonal, low and close to the 'u' bottom-edge label, so it reads as annotating the lower-left region rather than sitting mid-diagonal above the crossing as in the source.
Right panel's 'u − v' label is likewise shifted to the upper-left third of the descending diagonal instead of near its midpoint/crossing point as printed.
The 'v' label in the left panel is drawn inside the parallelogram beside the slanted edge; in the source it sits clearly outside, to the right of the edge.

Overall parallelograms render flatter/wider than the source (source shapes are a bit taller relative to their base), and the pair sits low-left in a large empty canvas rather than filling the frame as in the printed figure.
A dashed peach 'ghost v' arrow (with its own label) is added in the guided difference states — not present in the source (only visible after stepping, so low impact).
evaluation.notes: Structurally faithful two-panel parallelogram-rule figure with correct navy frames, thin diagonals and orange resultant/edge arrows plus rich, genuinely useful interactions (step player, reverse-v toggle, construction stepper, clickable diagonals); the main weakness is label placement — 'u + v' and 'u − v' sit off-centre near other labels instead of mid-diagonal, and 'v' is inside rather than outside the edge.
action_items: Move the resultant labels to ~0.5 along each diagonal with a perpendicular offset clear of the crossing, matching the printed positions, and ensure 'u + v' is not visually adjacent to the bottom 'u' label.
Place the left-panel 'v' label outside the slanted edge (to the right) as in the source, and check the −v label side likewise.
Scale the drawing to fill the available canvas width/height (reduce margins or increase world scale) so the two parallelograms are not stranded in the upper-left of a large empty area.
Suppress the dashed 'ghost v' and its label in any state that mimics the textbook view so the default read is a drop-in replacement.
